comparator.name: BSc Econometrics and Operations Research
comparator.sourceNotes: The official programme page presents a complete 180-EC curriculum: 60 EC in Year 1, 60 EC in Year 2 and 60 EC in Year 3. It names Econometrics, Operations Research, Actuarial Science and Mathematical Economics as profiles but presents one shared curriculum table rather than separate formal 180-EC routes, so no profile is instantiated as the comparator route. The 30-EC minor or study-abroad semester and the 5-EC programme elective remain explicit open-choice components.

progressionAssessment.rationale: Programming, economics and corporate-finance foundations begin in Semester 1. Mathematical Methods and Research Methods precede linear algebra, probability, econometrics and advanced quantitative work. Algorithms & Data Structures precedes Advanced Algorithms, and the main mathematical and programming foundations precede optimisation and reinforcement learning. Every formal prerequisite occurs earlier and every course is offered in its assigned term.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The closest curriculum covers the shared mathematical, statistical, econometric and economic core. The official Operations Research profile supports a distinct computational optimisation route, while the Mathematical Economics profile and programme-supported climate, welfare and public-policy problems support a distinct quantitative sustainability-and-policy route. The Actuarial Science direction was assessed separately but is not feasible because UCR lacks actuarial mathematics and insurance-risk courses. Three defensible alternatives are included, which is the maximum.

notes.text: Groningen provides a sustained specialist sequence in mathematics, econometrics, operations research and insurance. UCR can combine strong related courses in these areas, but does not reproduce the same disciplinary depth or actuarial sequence.
